## Study Overview

This project combines two complementary prediction models targeting different geographic scales and use cases:

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6}
### Arm 1 — Southeast Asia Provinces
A spatiotemporally-aware deep learning model (ST-GAT + GRU) trained on 162 admin-1 provinces across 10 SEA countries (2011–2018). It captures international dengue risk dynamics using province-level historical infection data, monthly climatological data (ERA5-Land, MODIS, CHIRPS), and Shared Socioeconomic Pathways. Inference runs monthly; the climate-only risk map is bias-corrected for the observed post-2018 climate shift.

[View SEA Provinces Results →](sea-provinces-study-results.qmd)
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
### Arm 2 — Taiwan Basic Statistics Area (BSA)
A Taiwan-specific counterpart operating at the finer granularity of the Basic Statistics Area (BSA) — the smallest census unit tracked by the Taiwanese government. It jointly considers international mobility (using SEA risk states from Arm 1 as exporter signals), local mobility, BSA-level environmental suitability, and population demographics to predict elevated local dengue risk.

[View Taiwan BSA Results →](taiwan-bsa-study-results.qmd)
:::

:::

## SEA Provinces — Current Risk Map

Predicted dengue incidence rate (relative risk index) for admin-1 regions across Southeast Asia.
Values > 1 indicate elevated risk relative to the 2011–2018 training baseline.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-risk-map
#| fig-cap: "Predicted relative dengue risk index (climate-only model). Inputs are corrected for the observed shift between 2011–2018 and 2019–2026 climate."

import json, pathlib
import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd

data_dir = pathlib.Path("data")
preds_path = data_dir / "latest_predictions.json"

preds = json.loads(preds_path.read_text()) if preds_path.exists() else {}
regions = preds.get("regions", {})
if not regions:
    print("⚠️  No prediction data found — run site/scripts/run_inference.py first.")
else:
    df = pd.DataFrame([
        {"region": k, "country": v["country"], "risk_index": v["risk_index"]}
        for k, v in regions.items()
    ])

    fig = px.choropleth(
        df,
        locations="country",
        locationmode="country names",
        color="risk_index",
        hover_name="region",
        hover_data={"risk_index": ":.2f", "country": True},
        color_continuous_scale="RdYlGn_r",
        range_color=[0, 3],
        labels={"risk_index": "Risk Index"},
        title=f"Dengue Risk Index — {preds.get('target_month', '')}",
        scope="asia",
    )
    fig.update_layout(margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=40, b=0), height=480)
    fig.show()
```

## SEA Provinces — Incidence-based Forecasts

The study model, IR + environment (`cyclical_seasonal`), shares its architecture with the climate-only model above and forecasts next month's incidence rate from the past 12 months of reported incidence plus climate and land use. It appears here when recent case data is supplied.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: tbl-incidence-forecasts
#| tbl-cap: "Predicted incidence rate (cases per 100,000) and risk index from the IR + environment model, highest predicted IR first."

import json, pathlib
import pandas as pd

data_dir = pathlib.Path("data")
models = {"ir_env": "IR + environment"}
loaded = {k: json.loads((data_dir / f"latest_predictions_{k}.json").read_text())
          for k in models if (data_dir / f"latest_predictions_{k}.json").exists()}

if not loaded:
    print("No incidence-based forecasts yet — they need site/data/incidence/recent_incidence.csv "
          "(see site/data/incidence/README.md).")
else:
    frames = []
    for key, preds in loaded.items():
        frames.append(pd.DataFrame([
            {"Province": name, "Country": r["country"],
             f"Predicted IR ({models[key]})": r["predicted_ir"],
             f"Risk index ({models[key]})": r["risk_index"]}
            for name, r in preds["regions"].items()
        ]).set_index(["Province", "Country"]))
    table = pd.concat(frames, axis=1)
    table = table.sort_values(table.columns[0], ascending=False).reset_index()
    months = {models[k]: p["target_month"] for k, p in loaded.items()}
    print("Forecast month: " + ", ".join(f"{m} ({name})" for name, m in months.items()))
    display(table.head(20).round(2))
```

## SEA Provinces — Risk Index Trends

Mean risk index across all SEA admin-1 regions over every month predictions have been archived.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-trends
#| fig-cap: "Monthly mean relative risk index across all SEA admin-1 regions. Values > 1 indicate elevated risk vs the 2011–2018 baseline."

import json, pathlib
import plotly.graph_objects as go

archive_dir = pathlib.Path("data/predictions/climate")
records = []
for f in sorted(archive_dir.glob("*.json")):
    data = json.loads(f.read_text())
    regions = data.get("regions", {})
    valid = [r["risk_index"] for r in regions.values() if r.get("has_data") and r.get("risk_index") is not None]
    if valid:
        records.append({
            "month": data["target_month"],
            "mean_risk": round(sum(valid) / len(valid), 4),
            "n_regions": len(valid),
        })

if not records:
    print("No archived predictions yet — will populate after the first monthly run.")
else:
    months = [r["month"] for r in records]
    means  = [r["mean_risk"] for r in records]

    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=months, y=means, mode="lines+markers",
        line=dict(color="#e63946", width=2),
        marker=dict(size=6),
        name="Mean risk index",
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>Risk index: %{y:.3f}<extra></extra>",
    ))
    fig.add_hline(y=1.0, line_dash="dash", line_color="grey",
                  annotation_text="Baseline (2011–2018 mean)", annotation_position="bottom right")
    fig.update_layout(
        xaxis_title="Month", yaxis_title="Mean Risk Index",
        height=320, margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=20, b=0),
    )
    fig.show()
```

## About

Dengue fever's transmission dynamics in Southeast Asia relies on human and vector mobility, displaying a high
degree of non-linearity and unpredictability. Moreover, as dengue outbreaks in Taiwan are
attributed to imported cases from Southeast Asia coinciding with windows of time where weather
favors vector reproductability, preventative measures must be taken at the right time in the right places.
To address the limits of considering dengue outbreak in isolation which ignores how circulating dengue serotypes
confer patterns that may only be explained across multiple countries extended beyond neighboring years,
this study creates a two-pronged experimental design that combines:
(1) a Southeast Asian spatiotemporally-aware deep learning
prediction model that captures international dengue risk dynamics based on province-level historical infection
data, near-real-time climatological data, as well as Shared Socioeconomic Pathways data.
(2) a Taiwan-only counterpart whose prediction works at a finer granularity, a Basic Statistics Area (BSA), and
predicts based on individual case report, clinical diagnosis, demographic data, and environmental data.

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-6}
### SEA Provinces Pipeline
1. Monthly zonal statistics fetched from Google Earth Engine
2. Observational climate delta (2019–2026 vs 2011–2018) applied to adjust for post-2018 climate shift
3. STGNN inference run on adjusted features
4. Results published automatically via GitHub Actions

**Architecture:** ST-GAT + GRU (PyTorch Geometric)
**Training period:** 2011–2018
**Features:** ERA5-Land, MODIS LST, NDVI/EVI, CHIRPS, LULC, WorldPop, SSP population
**Spatial scope:** 162 admin-1 regions across 10 SEA countries
**Performance (test set):** Huber 0.390 · MAE 1.214 · RMSE 2.460 (log IR, 14 held-out months)
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
### Taiwan BSA Pipeline
1. SEA province risk states ingested as international mobility proxy (from Arm 1)
2. BSA-level environmental suitability computed from TCCIP climate data
3. Individual case reports and demographic data from Taiwan Ministry of Health
4. BSA model inference generates sub-district risk predictions

**Architecture:** *(to be finalised)*
**Training period:** *(to be determined)*
**Features:** MoH case reports, clinical diagnosis, demographics, TCCIP climate, local mobility
**Spatial scope:** Taiwan Basic Statistics Areas (BSAs)
**Performance:** *(pending model training)*
:::

:::

---

> **Interpretation note:** SEA predictions are expressed as a *relative risk index* (predicted log IR normalised to the 2011–2018 baseline), not absolute case counts. This accounts for structural model uncertainty arising from the 8-year gap between training data and current conditions.
